value.title: Prebind identity validation and compatibility

sections.name: body
sections.value:
# Validate the identity that will actually be stored

The #182 review distinguished a runtime's candidate id from the final registry identity. A spawned child can register with a noncanonical candidate that is discarded when its correlated prebind is selected. Rejecting that candidate before target selection would break valid binding. Validate the final id whenever a registration would mint a row; when it updates an existing row, preserve that row's id and never store the discarded candidate.

Trace every creator separately. Explicit nonblank spawn ids are checked before lookup or launch; generated spawn names must satisfy the grammar. Adopt selects or mints through registration. Revive names an existing row, link changes parent/role, and federation aliases are view metadata rather than local-id renames. A public storage helper's ability to accept an arbitrary descriptor does not prove a production API can mint it.

Keep refusal contracts precise. Empty/whitespace spawn ids deliberately retain the older generic nonempty-argument refusal; nonblank malformed ids receive E-RS-SEAT-ID. Documentation must qualify that distinction instead of implying one code covers both. Render-time validation still protects older stored ids. Neither target selection nor a closed grammar proves caller ownership; that is the separate capability issuer's job.
